question.en: Do I Qualify for Medicare Extra Help (LIS) in Oklahoma in 2026?
question.es: ¿Califico para la Ayuda Adicional de Medicare (LIS) en Oklahoma en 2026?

shortAnswer.en: Yes, if income is under $23,940 (individual) or $32,460 (couple) in 2026.
shortAnswer.es: Sí, si sus ingresos son menores a $23,940 (individual) o $32,460 (pareja) en 2026.

fullAnswer.en: Yes. Oklahoma Medicare beneficiaries qualify for Extra Help in 2026 with income below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level, $23,940 for a single person or $32,460 for a married couple, and resources under $16,590 single or $33,100 married. Oklahomans already enrolled in full SoonerCare, SSI, or an OHCA-run Medicare Savings Program (QMB, SLMB, or QI) are deemed eligible automatically. Everyone else applies through Social Security or MySoonerCare.org.
fullAnswer.es: Sí. Los beneficiarios de Medicare en Oklahoma califican para la Ayuda Adicional en 2026 con ingresos menores al 150% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza, $23,940 para una persona soltera o $32,460 para una pareja casada, y recursos menores a $16,590 soltero o $33,100 casado. Los residentes de Oklahoma ya inscritos en SoonerCare completo, SSI, o un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare administrado por OHCA son elegibles automáticamente.

h1.en: Medicare Extra Help (LIS) and SoonerCare in Oklahoma (2026)
h1.es: Ayuda Adicional de Medicare (LIS) y SoonerCare en Oklahoma (2026)

introParagraphs.en: Oklahoma has roughly 780,000 Medicare beneficiaries, and a meaningful share of them qualify for Extra Help, the federal Low-Income Subsidy (LIS) that pays most of the Part D premium, waives the deductible, and caps drug copays at $5.10 generic or $12.65 brand-name in 2026. The income and resource limits for Extra Help are set nationally by the Social Security Administration, but Oklahoma residents have a distinct path into the program through SoonerCare, the state's Medicaid program administered by the Oklahoma Health Care Authority (OHCA), which automatically deems many low-income Oklahomans eligible.
introParagraphs.es: Oklahoma tiene aproximadamente 780,000 beneficiarios de Medicare, y una parte significativa califica para la Ayuda Adicional, el Subsidio Federal de Bajos Ingresos (LIS) que paga la mayor parte de la prima de la Parte D, elimina el deducible y limita los copagos de medicamentos a $5.10 generico o $12.65 de marca en 2026. Los limites de ingresos y recursos los fija la Administracion del Seguro Social a nivel nacional, pero los residentes de Oklahoma tienen una via distinta hacia el programa a traves de SoonerCare, el programa Medicaid del estado administrado por la Autoridad de Atencion Medica de Oklahoma (OHCA), que califica automaticamente a muchos residentes de bajos ingresos.

introParagraphs.en: Oklahoma residents will find the exact 2026 Extra Help income limits by household size below, along with how SoonerCare enrollment or an OHCA-run Medicare Savings Program grants automatic eligibility, and the step-by-step application process for those who need to apply directly. For income limits on Oklahoma's Medicaid program itself, see [Medicaid income limits](/en/medicaid-income-limits). To check multiple programs at once, use the [Benefits Screener](/en/screener).
introParagraphs.es: Esta pagina detalla los limites exactos de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional de 2026 por tamano de hogar, como la inscripcion en SoonerCare o un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare administrado por OHCA otorga elegibilidad automatica, y el proceso de solicitud paso a paso para los residentes de Oklahoma que necesitan solicitar directamente.

heading.es: Respuesta Directa para Residentes de Oklahoma

paragraphs.en: Yes. Oklahoma Medicare beneficiaries qualify for Extra Help in 2026 if household income is below 150% of the Federal Poverty Level ($23,940 single, $32,460 married) and countable resources stay under $16,590 single or $33,100 married. Oklahomans on full SoonerCare, SSI, or an OHCA Medicare Savings Program are deemed eligible automatically, with no separate application required.
paragraphs.es: Sí. Los beneficiarios de Medicare en Oklahoma califican para la Ayuda Adicional en 2026 si el ingreso del hogar es menor al 150% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza ($23,940 soltero, $32,460 casado) y los recursos contables son menores a $16,590 soltero o $33,100 casado.

heading.en: Oklahoma Extra Help Income Limits by Household Size (2026)
heading.es: Limites de Ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional en Oklahoma por Tamano del Hogar (2026)

paragraphs.en: Oklahoma uses the same nationwide Extra Help income thresholds that apply in all 48 contiguous states and D.C., since Oklahoma is not Alaska or Hawaii (the two states with higher federal poverty guidelines). The table below shows the 2026 limits at 150% of the Federal Poverty Level for every household size, along with the monthly equivalent Oklahoma applicants can compare against a pay stub or Social Security award letter.
paragraphs.es: Oklahoma usa los mismos umbrales de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional a nivel nacional que aplican en los 48 estados contiguos y D.C., ya que Oklahoma no es Alaska ni Hawaii. La tabla siguiente muestra los limites de 2026 al 150% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza para cada tamano de hogar.

heading.en: Federal Resource (Asset) Limits for Extra Help in Oklahoma (2026)
heading.es: Limites de Recursos (Activos) Federales para la Ayuda Adicional en Oklahoma (2026)

paragraphs.en: Oklahoma applicants for the federal Extra Help program must also pass a resource test: countable assets below $16,590 for a single person or $33,100 for a married couple in 2026. Countable resources include checking and savings accounts, CDs, stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and IRA or 401(k) balances not yet in payout status. An Oklahoma applicant's home, one vehicle, and personal belongings do not count toward the limit.
paragraphs.es: Los solicitantes en Oklahoma para el programa federal de Ayuda Adicional tambien deben pasar una prueba de recursos: activos contables por debajo de $16,590 para una persona soltera o $33,100 para una pareja casada en 2026. Los recursos contables incluyen cuentas corrientes y de ahorro, CD, acciones, bonos, fondos mutuos y saldos de IRA o 401(k).

paragraphs.en: Oklahoma's own Medicare Savings Programs, run separately by OHCA under SoonerCare, use a lower state resource limit of $9,950 for an individual or $14,910 for a couple in 2026. A 2025 federal budget reconciliation law paused further implementation of a CMS rule that would have aligned every state's Medicare Savings Program resource test with the higher federal Extra Help limit through at least 2034, so Oklahoma's QMB, SLMB, and QI asset tests remain lower than the Extra Help test used by Social Security.
paragraphs.es: Los Programas de Ahorros de Medicare propios de Oklahoma, administrados por separado por OHCA bajo SoonerCare, usan un limite de recursos estatal mas bajo de $9,950 para una persona o $14,910 para una pareja en 2026. Una ley federal de reconciliacion presupuestaria de 2025 pauso la implementacion adicional de una regla de CMS que habria alineado la prueba de recursos con el limite federal de Ayuda Adicional hasta al menos 2034.

heading.en: SoonerCare, OHCA Medicare Savings Programs, and Automatic Eligibility in Oklahoma
heading.es: SoonerCare, Programas de Ahorros de Medicare de OHCA y Elegibilidad Automatica en Oklahoma

paragraphs.en: SoonerCare is Oklahoma's Medicaid program, administered by the Oklahoma Health Care Authority (OHCA), and OHCA plays a direct role in Extra Help eligibility, not just Medicaid coverage. Oklahomans who have full SoonerCare coverage, receive Supplemental Security Income, or are enrolled in an OHCA Medicare Savings Program (QMB, SLMB, or QI, sometimes called SoonerCare Supplemental for dual eligibles) are deemed eligible for Extra Help automatically. OHCA sends the eligibility file to CMS, and no separate SSA application is needed for these Oklahomans.
paragraphs.es: SoonerCare es el programa Medicaid de Oklahoma, administrado por la Autoridad de Atencion Medica de Oklahoma (OHCA), y OHCA juega un papel directo en la elegibilidad para la Ayuda Adicional, no solo en la cobertura de Medicaid. Los residentes de Oklahoma que tienen cobertura completa de SoonerCare, reciben Ingreso de Seguridad Suplementaria, o estan inscritos en un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare de OHCA son elegibles automaticamente para la Ayuda Adicional.

paragraphs.en: Oklahoma voters approved Medicaid expansion through State Question 802 on June 30, 2020, and coverage for newly eligible adults began July 1, 2021, making Oklahoma the 37th state to expand Medicaid under the ACA. Low-income Oklahoma adults ages 19 to 64 under 138% FPL (138% of the Federal Poverty Level, about $22,176 a year for one person under OHCA's 2026 SoonerCare chart) generally qualify for SoonerCare Medicaid itself, not just Extra Help. Because Oklahoma expanded, the state does not have the ACA coverage gap that exists in the 10 non-expansion states (Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Wisconsin, and Wyoming). Extra Help uses a separate, higher 150% FPL income test and counts gross income directly, unlike SoonerCare and ACA marketplace subsidies which use MAGI (Modified Adjusted Gross Income).
paragraphs.es: Los votantes de Oklahoma aprobaron la expansion de Medicaid mediante la Pregunta Estatal 802 el 30 de junio de 2020, y la cobertura para los adultos recien elegibles comenzo el 1 de julio de 2021, convirtiendo a Oklahoma en el estado numero 37 en expandir Medicaid bajo el ACA. Los adultos de bajos ingresos en Oklahoma de 19 a 64 anos por debajo del 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza (unos $22,176 al ano para una persona) generalmente califican para Medicaid de SoonerCare. Debido a que Oklahoma expandio, el estado no tiene la brecha de cobertura del ACA.

heading.en: How Oklahoma Residents Apply for Extra Help
heading.es: Como Solicitan los Residentes de Oklahoma la Ayuda Adicional

paragraphs.en: Oklahoma residents who are not already deemed eligible through SoonerCare, SSI, or an OHCA Medicare Savings Program can apply for Extra Help through two channels: directly with Social Security, or through the state's application portal, MySoonerCare.org, which also screens for SoonerCare Medicaid and Medicare Savings Programs.
paragraphs.es: Los residentes de Oklahoma que aun no son elegibles automaticamente a traves de SoonerCare, SSI o un Programa de Ahorros de Medicare de OHCA pueden solicitar la Ayuda Adicional a traves de dos canales: directamente con el Seguro Social, o a traves del portal de solicitud del estado, MySoonerCare.org.

heading.en: Common Reasons Extra Help Applications Get Denied in Oklahoma
heading.es: Razones Comunes por las que se Niegan Solicitudes en Oklahoma

paragraphs.en: Oklahoma applicants who apply directly through Social Security or MySoonerCare.org are denied for a handful of predictable reasons, most of which can be corrected and resubmitted. Household income or countable resources over the limit are the two most common causes, followed by missing documentation of income or household composition.
paragraphs.es: Los solicitantes de Oklahoma que aplican directamente a traves del Seguro Social o MySoonerCare.org son rechazados por razones predecibles, la mayoria corregibles y reenviables. Ingresos del hogar o recursos contables por encima del limite son las dos causas mas comunes, seguidas de documentacion faltante.

list.es: Ingreso del hogar por encima del 150% del FPL una vez combinados los ingresos de todos los miembros

heading.en: How to Appeal a Denial in Oklahoma
heading.es: Como Apelar una Negacion en Oklahoma

paragraphs.en: An Oklahoma applicant denied Extra Help by Social Security has 60 days to request reconsideration in writing, either by mail or at a local Social Security field office. If the denial came from OHCA because the application was filed through MySoonerCare.org, the applicant has 30 days from the notice to file Form LD-1 for an administrative appeal, and free help is available from the Oklahoma Insurance Department's State Health Insurance Counseling Program (SHIP) at 1-800-522-0071.
paragraphs.es: Un solicitante de Oklahoma a quien se le niega la Ayuda Adicional por el Seguro Social tiene 60 dias para solicitar una reconsideracion por escrito, ya sea por correo o en una oficina local del Seguro Social. Si la negacion vino de OHCA porque la solicitud se presento por MySoonerCare.org, el solicitante tiene 30 dias desde el aviso para presentar el Formulario LD-1.

heading.es: Contexto de SoonerCare: la Agencia de Medicaid de Oklahoma

paragraphs.en: SoonerCare has covered Oklahomans since the state's Medicaid program was established under federal law, and today it covers more than 1.1 million Oklahomans, including low-income families, pregnant individuals, children, and adults under the State Question 802 expansion group. For Medicare beneficiaries specifically, OHCA also runs Oklahoma's Medicare Savings Programs (QMB, SLMB, and QI), which pay Part B premiums and, for QMB enrollees, cost-sharing, and which double as an automatic gateway into Extra Help.
paragraphs.es: SoonerCare ha cubierto a los residentes de Oklahoma desde que se establecio el programa Medicaid del estado bajo la ley federal, y hoy cubre a mas de 1.1 millones de residentes de Oklahoma, incluidas familias de bajos ingresos, personas embarazadas, ninos y adultos bajo el grupo de expansion de la Pregunta Estatal 802. Para los beneficiarios de Medicare especificamente, OHCA tambien administra los Programas de Ahorros de Medicare de Oklahoma.

en.question: What is the Extra Help income limit for a family of 4 in Oklahoma in 2026?
en.answer: In 2026, an Oklahoma household of 4 qualifies for Extra Help with income below $49,500 a year ($4,125 a month). This is the same nationwide limit used in every state except Alaska and Hawaii, since Extra Help thresholds are set federally by Social Security rather than by OHCA.

en.question: What counts as income for Extra Help in Oklahoma?
en.answer: Extra Help counts gross income before taxes, including Social Security benefits, wages, pensions, and rental income, with a few exclusions. This differs from MAGI (Modified Adjusted Gross Income), the calculation SoonerCare Medicaid and ACA marketplace subsidies use, so an Oklahoma resident's Extra Help eligibility and SoonerCare eligibility can differ even at similar income levels.

en.question: What documents do Oklahoma applicants need for Extra Help?
en.answer: Oklahoma applicants need a Social Security number or Medicare card, recent tax returns or W-2s, bank and investment statements, proof of any other income, proof of Oklahoma residency, and household composition documentation. Applying through MySoonerCare.org can pull some records automatically, but income and asset statements are still required.

en.question: What happens if my Extra Help application is denied in Oklahoma?
en.answer: An Oklahoma applicant denied by Social Security has 60 days to request reconsideration in writing. If denied by OHCA after applying via MySoonerCare.org, the applicant has 30 days to file Form LD-1 for an administrative appeal. Free help is available from the Oklahoma Insurance Department's SHIP program.

en.question: Can I work and still get Extra Help in Oklahoma?
en.answer: Yes, working does not disqualify an Oklahoma resident from Extra Help as long as total gross household income stays below the 2026 limit for the household size, $23,940 for one person or $32,460 for a couple. Wages are counted as income the same as Social Security or pension income.

en.question: Is Oklahoma a Medicaid expansion state, and does that matter for Extra Help?
en.answer: Yes. Oklahoma expanded Medicaid under the ACA effective July 1, 2021, through State Question 802, covering adults ages 19 to 64 up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level (about $22,176 for an individual in 2026). Because Oklahoma expanded, there is no ACA coverage gap, and many SoonerCare-eligible adults who later enroll in Medicare are deemed automatically eligible for Extra Help.

en.question: How long does the Extra Help application take for Oklahoma residents?
en.answer: Social Security typically decides an Extra Help application within 30 to 60 days of receiving all required documents. Applications submitted through MySoonerCare.org that also screen for SoonerCare Medicaid can take a similar timeframe, since OHCA coordinates its determination with the federal Extra Help decision.

en.question: What is the difference between SoonerCare and Medicare Extra Help?
en.answer: SoonerCare is Oklahoma's state Medicaid agency program, covering low-income residents of all ages for medical, dental, and long-term care services. Medicare Extra Help is a separate federal program that only reduces Medicare Part D prescription drug costs. Oklahomans with full SoonerCare coverage or an OHCA Medicare Savings Program get Extra Help automatically as a bonus benefit.

es.question: Cual es el limite de ingresos de la Ayuda Adicional para una familia de 4 en Oklahoma en 2026?
es.answer: En 2026, un hogar de Oklahoma de 4 personas califica para la Ayuda Adicional con ingresos menores a $49,500 al ano ($4,125 al mes). Este es el mismo limite nacional usado en todos los estados excepto Alaska y Hawaii.

es.question: Que cuenta como ingreso para la Ayuda Adicional en Oklahoma?
es.answer: La Ayuda Adicional cuenta el ingreso bruto antes de impuestos, incluidos los beneficios del Seguro Social, salarios, pensiones e ingresos por alquiler, con algunas exclusiones. Esto difiere del MAGI, el calculo que usan SoonerCare Medicaid y los subsidios del mercado del ACA.

es.question: Que documentos necesitan los solicitantes de Oklahoma para la Ayuda Adicional?
es.answer: Los solicitantes de Oklahoma necesitan un numero de Seguro Social o tarjeta de Medicare, declaraciones de impuestos recientes o W-2, estados de cuenta bancarios y de inversion, prueba de otros ingresos, prueba de residencia en Oklahoma y documentacion de composicion del hogar.

es.question: Que pasa si se niega mi solicitud de Ayuda Adicional en Oklahoma?
es.answer: Un solicitante de Oklahoma a quien se le niega por el Seguro Social tiene 60 dias para solicitar una reconsideracion por escrito. Si OHCA la niega despues de solicitar por MySoonerCare.org, el solicitante tiene 30 dias para presentar el Formulario LD-1.

es.question: Puedo trabajar y aun recibir la Ayuda Adicional en Oklahoma?
es.answer: Si, trabajar no descalifica a un residente de Oklahoma de la Ayuda Adicional siempre que el ingreso bruto total del hogar se mantenga por debajo del limite de 2026 para el tamano del hogar, $23,940 para una persona o $32,460 para una pareja.

es.question: Es Oklahoma un estado de expansion de Medicaid, y eso importa para la Ayuda Adicional?
es.answer: Si. Oklahoma expandio Medicaid bajo el ACA a partir del 1 de julio de 2021, mediante la Pregunta Estatal 802, cubriendo a adultos de 19 a 64 anos hasta el 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza (unos $22,176 para un individuo en 2026). Debido a que Oklahoma expandio, no hay brecha de cobertura del ACA.

es.question: Cuanto tiempo toma la solicitud de Ayuda Adicional para los residentes de Oklahoma?
es.answer: El Seguro Social generalmente decide una solicitud de Ayuda Adicional dentro de 30 a 60 dias de recibir todos los documentos requeridos. Las solicitudes enviadas por MySoonerCare.org que tambien evaluan Medicaid de SoonerCare pueden tomar un tiempo similar.

es.question: Cual es la diferencia entre SoonerCare y la Ayuda Adicional de Medicare?
es.answer: SoonerCare es el programa estatal de Medicaid de Oklahoma, que cubre a residentes de bajos ingresos de todas las edades para servicios medicos, dentales y de cuidado a largo plazo. La Ayuda Adicional de Medicare es un programa federal separado que solo reduce los costos de medicamentos de la Parte D.
